newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy price trend may change--Labor official.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy price trend may change--Labor official.

text.p: A U.S. Department of Labor economist said on Thursday the beneficial impact of low or decreasing energy prices on the overall inflation rate may soon be over.

"It has been favorable as far as holding down inflation," Patrick Jackman told Reuters Financial Television. "There is some concern however based upon secondary data that this trend may soon be ending here."
The economist added, however, that he did not expect any substantial increases in energy prices either.
"No one is looking for a big, sharp increase in energy prices," he said.

The Labor Department earlier said overall consumer prices in July had risen 0.2 percent in July, after an 0.1 increase in the previous month. The consumer price index's energy component fell 0.1 percent after being unchanged in June.
